title: Landslide & Mudslide Safety Guide
summary: Landslides occur rapidly on steep slopes after heavy rainfall or earthquakes. Move away from the path of debris immediately.
precautions: Watch for warning signs: tilting trees, new cracks in soil/pavement, or sudden mudflow streams.
Listen for unusual sounds like trees cracking or boulders knocking together.
If near a stream or channel, be alert for sudden changes in water clarity (clear to muddy).
Evacuate slope areas immediately during intense prolonged rainfall.
evacuation: Move quickly perpendicular to the direction of the slide path (run sideways, not downhill).
Reach high, stable ground or solid rock formations away from steep hillsides.
Avoid river valleys and low-lying gullies where mudslides funnel.
firstAid: Check for trapped victims near the edge of the slide area without endangering yourself.
Treat crush injuries and broken limbs with immobilization and immediate medical transport.
Keep hypothermia and shock victims warm with blankets.
emergencyChecklist: Sturdy hiking boots with non-slip soles
First aid kit and emergency blanket
dos: DO run sideways away from the path of mudflow.
DO curl into a tight ball protecting your head if caught in debris.
DO report cracked roads or mud movement to authorities.
donts: DON'T cross flooded bridges or mud-covered mountain roads.
DON'T stay inside structures in direct line of steep hill slopes.
DON'T return to slide area until geologists clear it safe.
